business_scope.primary_industry_name: Publishing of Lightweight Ad-Monetized Mobile Games

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Continental code-based system with cantonal procedural variants at the Commercial Register and notarial levels)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Swiss-US Double Taxation Agreement (signed 1996, as amended by the 2019 Protocol)
Swiss-UK Double Taxation Agreement (1977, as amended by the Multilateral Instrument ratified 2021)
Switzerland-Germany Double Taxation Agreement (1971, as amended by the 2010 protocol)
Switzerland-France Double Taxation Agreement (1966, as amended)
Switzerland-China Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 1986, in force 1987)
EFTA Convention (Stockholm Convention, 1960, as updated by the Vaduz Convention 2001)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Bundesgesetz über die Bekämpfung der Geldwäscherei und der Terrorismusfinanzierung (Geldwäschereigesetz, GwG) of 10 October 1997 (SR 955.0), particularly Arts. 3, 6, 9, 10 and 37; Swiss Criminal Code (StGB, SR 311.0) Arts. 305bis, 305ter and 260quinquies; Swiss Code of Obligations (OR, SR 220) Arts. 626, 627, 651, 697i and 952; Money Laundering Ordinance FINMA (GwV-FINMA, SR 955.011); Swiss Commercial Register Ordinance (HRegV, SR 221.411); Swiss Federal Act on Swissness (LPM/Swissness Act, SR 232.11) and Trade Names Protection Act (SR 232.11).
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Private_Internal – Switzerland maintains no public UBO register; UBO declarations are kept privately by the company, notary, and financial intermediaries and are accessible upon lawful request to FINMA, MROS/SECO, the cantonal commercial registers, and the tax administration under the AEOI/CRS framework.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copy of each beneficial owner (founding shareholder/UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Local notary public or competent public administration in the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the country of origin is an Apostille Convention party; otherwise Consular Legalization through the Swiss Embassy/Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address of each UBO (utility bill, bank statement, or residence certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing utility company, bank, or municipal authority in the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or notarized copy with chain authentication under Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of legal existence / excerpt from the commercial register for any corporate UBO (parent entity)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry in the corporate UBO's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization for non-Apostille jurisdictions; translation into German, French, or Italian with certified translator declaration

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank confirmation of share capital deposit (Einlagebescheinigung / certificat de blocage de capital)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Swiss-regulated bank (SIX member) where the statutory minimum share capital of CHF 100,000 is deposited and blocked at the disposal of the notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic Swiss bank confirmation delivered directly to the notary; no apostille required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: CV and background declaration for each director and managing officer (for PEP/AML and commercial registry fitness assessment)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Director or managing officer personally, with signature certified by a notary or consular authority in the country of signing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization for signatures executed abroad; Swiss notarial authentication if signed in Switzerland

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against: (i) UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists; (ii) US OFAC SDN and Non-SDN consolidated lists; (iii) EU consolidated financial sanctions list; (iv) Switzerland's SECO sanctions measures ordered under the Federal Act on Embargoes (EmbG, SR 946.231) and the Swiss Criminal Code freezing measures; (v) UK HMT sanctions; and (vi) Interpol and domestic criminal records. PEP determination follows FATF standards and Swiss bank-AML practice: any individual holding a prominent public function, their family members, and close associates require enhanced due diligence and documented senior-management approval before the shareholder contribution is accepted and the corporate bank account is opened.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: ZEFIX – Zentraler Firmenindex (Central Company Index) at www.zefix.ch; official clearance is effected through the competent cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the target canton, with subsequent publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be consistent with the official language of the canton of the registered office (German, French, or Italian), must use Latin script, and must comply with Art. 950 of the Swiss Code of Obligations (truthfulness, distinctiveness, no misleading elements). Foreign-language names are permissible only when written in Latin letters and are examined for general comprehensibility in Switzerland. The suffix 'AG' or 'SA' must reflect the legal form and language regime of the articles of association.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Schweiz / Schweizer / Swiss / Suisse / Svizzero (Swissness indication restricted under the Swissness Act and Art. 47 LPM)
Bank / Bankier / Private Banking (banking license under the Swiss Financial Institutions Act required)
Versicherung / Assurance / Assicurazione (insurance supervision license required)
Treuhand / Fiduciaire / Trust (prior approval by the competent supervisory authority required; licensed fiduciary conduct)
Fonds / Fondation d'investissement (CISA license and FINMA approval required)
Anwalt / Rechtsanwalt / Avocat (compliance with the Swiss Lawyers Act required)
Zürich / Genève / Zug (cantonal and municipal names requiring consent of the respective authority)
Eidgenössisch / Confédéral (official federal character requiring governmental authorization)
Spar / Kredit / Darlehen (consumer financial services regulated under the Swiss Consumer Credit Act)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Once an application is rejected, the cantonal Commercial Register Office must issue a written refusal stating the grounds. The applicant may submit a revised name without payment of a new register fee within 30 days, or file a formal administrative appeal to the cantonal supervisory authority (kantonale Aufsichtsbehörde über das Handelsregister) within 30 days of the refusal. A further appeal lies to the Federal Administrative Court (Bundesverwaltungsgericht, BVGer) in Bern. In parallel, a fresh name-reservation request with amended tokens may be filed; no legal counsel is required but is recommended where Swissness or regulated tokens are involved.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual-office mailbox arrangement is not permissible for a Swiss Aktiengesellschaft. The registered office (Sitz) must correspond to the place of actual administration within Switzerland (Art. 56 of the Swiss Civil Code ZGB and Art. 626 para. 2 OR). For an ISIC 5820 hyper-casual games company operating a remote digital model, a credible physical seat in Switzerland—or a licensed domiciliation provider in the target canton providing a full registered-office service (records, registered mail, corporate minutes, and board facilities)—is mandatory. Domiciliation arrangements are accepted only where actual administrative substance, board decision-making, and accounting records are demonstrably located in Switzerland; otherwise the entity risks reclassification as a mere mailbox company by the tax administration and the commercial register.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: approximately 20% within the first 12 months if a pure domiciliation/shared-office arrangement is used; below 5% within the first 12 months if a dedicated physical office is leased in the target canton (e.g., Zug, Zurich, Geneva). Direct on-site inspections may be conducted by the cantonal Commercial Register Office, the cantonal tax administration, or FINMA-designated auditors without prior announcement for substance and AML verification.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cantonal notary public (tariff varies by canton; e.g., Zurich, Zug, Geneva)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Cantonal statutory notarial tariff, prevailing market rate CHF 2,500–3,500 depending on notional capital and scope of deed

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Cantonal Commercial Register entry fee (one-time, including federal share for the central registry index)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cantonal Handelsregisteramt (Commercial Register Office) receiving federal share via ZEFIX
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee schedule under the Federal Ordinance on Commercial Register Fees (GebV-HReg, SR 221.411)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB) incorporation publication fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory SHAB fee schedule per publication entry

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translations and language certification of foreign UBO and corporate documents (German/French/Italian)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per certified page/hourly rate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille certifications for foreign UBO documents (passport copies, address proofs, corporate excerpts) – up to 5 certificates
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent cantonal apostille authority (State Chancellery) or Federal Office of Justice for federal documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory cantonal fee per apostille (average CHF 25–30 per certificate)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO/AML/KYC screening of all beneficial owners, directors, and authorized signatories (PEP, OFAC, UN, EU, SECO, Interpol, criminal records)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office / domiciliation service with physical corporate seat, first year prepaid
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed domiciliation provider in target canton (Zug / Zurich / Geneva)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for annual registered-office and domiciliation services for an AG

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Stage-1 legal counsel: pre-incorporation structural due diligence, UBO piercing verification, notarial coordination, statutory-compliant drafting of incorporation documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing Swiss law firm hourly rate / fixed-stage fee, CHF 6,000–8,000

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank confirmation of share capital deposit (Einlagebescheinigung) issued by the Swiss depositary bank
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss-regulated bank holding the blocked CHF 100,000 minimum share capital
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank fee schedule for issuance of the capital-confirmation certificate under Art. 651 OR

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht / Code des obligations), Part Five, Stock Companies Law, Articles 620-763; specifically Art. 626 ff. (incorporation procedure), Art. 632 ff. (share capital and paid-up capital), Art. 640 (registered shares), and Art. 643 (Commercial Register entry). See also Art. 16 Bundesgesetz über die Amtliche Veröffentlichung/SHAB publication rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Register Office of the canton of the registered office (Handelsregisteramt / Registre du commerce), under cantonal register supervision and federal oversight of the Swiss Federal Office of Justice (BG-FOI/OFJ); national data indexed and searchable through the Zefix federal register portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized public deed of incorporation and Articles of Association (Statuten) together with the formal Application for Entry in the Commercial Register (Anmeldung zur Eintragung in das Handelsregister), filed electronically by the Swiss civil-law notary public.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Swiss AG minimum statutory share capital is CHF 100,000. At incorporation, at least 20% of the nominal value per share (i.e. CHF 20,000 on a CHF 100,000 capital) must be actually paid up and deposited in a blocked/escrow Swiss bank account (Sperrkonto) opened in the name of the formation company; the bank confirmation (Bankbestätigung) must be produced to the Commercial Register and the funds may be released only upon definitive registration. Contributions in kind require a statutory formation audit report; the unpaid balance is subject to a board call for payment.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Board of Directors of [Company] AG, having reviewed the public deed of incorporation executed before the Swiss notary, hereby: (1) approves and subscribes the share capital of CHF 100,000, divided into 100 registered shares of CHF 1,000 each, with CHF 20,000 paid up; (2) accepts the bank confirmation of the blocked capital deposit and authorizes its release upon issuance of the Commercial Register certificate; (3) adopts [Street No.], [City], canton [Code], Switzerland, as the statutory registered office; (4) appoints [A] as Chairperson, [B] as Member of the Board, and [C] as authorized signatory with individual signature authority; and (5) authorizes each director to effect and sign all applications, declarations and filings required for Commercial Register entry and subsequent UID and social insurance registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Search, Trade Name Pre-Approval, and Statutory Purpose Clause Drafting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) via the Zefix federal name index, with the founding Swiss notary public conducting the pre-filing legal review.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Run a Zefix federal search over the national company-name and trade-mark index to confirm that no identical or confusingly similar business name exists in Switzerland. Define a distinctive name element with the mandatory legal form suffix 'AG'/'SA'. Draft the business-purpose clause of the Articles of Association (Statuten) precisely to cover ISIC 5820 software publishing, hyper-casual mobile game development, advertising monetization, and ancillary license rights, in the official language of the registered-seat canton.
required_dossiers: Zefix name-search excerpt confirming name availability
Certified passports/identity documents of all founders
Business plan or purpose summary for ISIC 5820 hyper-casual game publishing
Registered-office address confirmation from the lease agreement or landlord consent
Power of attorney appointing the notary where any founder is absent (public deed or consular legalized paper power)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry objects to the proposed name or purpose clause, the notary submits a revised name proposal or a narrowed purpose clause for re-pre-approval within the same dossier at no additional fee. A second refusal may be appealed to the cantonal commercial register supervisory authority within 10 calendar days from notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Articles of Association and Execution of the Public Formation Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal civil-law notary public (öffentlicher Notar / notaire) holding deed authority in the canton of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founders appear before the Swiss notary to sign the Articles of Association (Statuten) and the public formation deed (Gründungsprotokoll / acte constitutif). The deed must state the company name, seat, purpose, share capital, share types and nominal amounts, board appointment, and the subscription of the fully paid and non-paid capital. The notary authenticates signatures, confirms legal capacity, and certifies the deed for onward transmission to the Commercial Register Office.
required_dossiers: Approved draft Articles of Association (Statuten) in the official language of the canton
Passports/identity cards of all founders and appointed board members
Name pre-approval or availability confirmation from the registry
Power of attorney for any absent founder signed before a Swiss notary or legalized abroad
Landlord consent or lease agreement for the registered office where required by the registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies formal defects, such as an incomplete capital clause or invalid seat expression, the deed is re-executed in a supplementary notarial session with a corrected annex; the initial deed is annulled and replaced without prejudice, and the corrected deed is then re-submitted for registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of Paid-up Share Capital in a Blocked Swiss Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: FINMA-regulated Swiss bank (e.g. UBS, Zürcher Kantonalbank, UBS Switzerland AG) acting as depository bank for the formation capital.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open an escrow/blocked account (Sperrkonto) in the exact name of the formation company. Deposit the cash contribution of CHF 20,000, representing at least 20% of the CHF 100,000 nominal share capital, and obtain the bank confirmation certificate (Bankbestätigung) evidencing that the funds are available, paid in by the contributors, and blocked until the definitive Commercial Register entry. The bank will release the funds but only upon presentation of the registration certificate or equivalent registry confirmation.
required_dossiers: Fully executed notarized incorporation deed and Statuten
Passports/identity cards of all board members and authorized signatories
Bank-standard AML/KYC and beneficial-owner identification forms
Company name approval/notarized deed extract as requested by the bank
Proof of address and source-of-funds statement for the CHF 20,000 contribution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the chosen bank refuses the account, the founders may substitute another FINMA-regulated bank and obtain a fresh bank confirmation. If the bank confirmation contains discrepancies, the bank issues an amended confirmation, and the Commercial Register accepts the corrected certificate without reopening the formation procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Register Filing and Statutory Registration (Handelsregistereintrag)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Registre du commerce) with subsequent official publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary files the Application for Entry in the Commercial Register (Anmeldung zur Eintragung) electronically, attaching the authenticated incorporation deed, the Articles of Association, the bank confirmation of the paid-up blocked capital, and the board acceptance declarations. The registry verifies the statutory formation prerequisites under Art. 626 ff. CO, confirms that the company name is lawful and distinguishable, and upon approval enters the AG in the register. The entry is then published in the SHAB, which constitutes valid third-party notice.
required_dossiers: Signed Application for Entry in the Commercial Register (Anmeldung)
Certified notarial copy of the incorporation deed and Articles of Association
Bank confirmation certificate for the paid-up blocked capital
Declarations of acceptance of office by board members and any statutory auditors
Identity documents and residence evidence of directors; sufficient connection documentation for non-resident directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a formal query or provisional refusal (Vormerkung), the notary files supplementary explanations and corrected documents within the statutory cure period of 20 days. If the entry is definitively refused, the company may appeal within 30 days to the cantonal administrative authority supervising the Commercial Register, and subsequently to the federal instance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: UID/VAT and Social Insurance (AHV) Registration and Post-Registration Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Federal Statistical Office (UID register), Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/AFC) for VAT, cantonal tax administration, and the cantonal AHV Compensation Office (Ausgleichskasse).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon Commercial Register entry, the Federal Statistical Office automatically issues the Swiss business identification number (UID). If the ad-monetized gaming services are subject to Swiss VAT, register for VAT with ESTV electronically, verifying the place-of-supply rules and reverse-charge treatment for payments from foreign ad networks such as AdMob and AppLovin. Register the company and employees with the AHV compensation office for old-age and survivors' insurance, and contract occupational accident and loss-of-earnings insurance with Suva or an approved private insurer.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register excerpt issued within 30 days containing the UID
VAT registration application and expected turnover statement
Certificate of incorporation from the Commercial Register
Shareholder and board resolutions confirming the operational seat and payroll arrangements
AHV social insurance registration questionnaire and payroll setup form
Corporate bank account details for tax and social contribution payments
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a registration is missed or delayed, simplified late registration may be filed with ESTV or the AHV compensation office directly. Any procedural penalties are limited to nominal administrative fines, and the UID remains valid for all tax and social security interactions once registration is completed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - no industrial operating license exists for ISIC 5820 software and hyper-casual game publishing; the Swiss Federal Institute of Intellectual Property (IGE/IPI) governs trademark and copyright matters but grants no operating license. Municipal business registration under cantonal trade legislation may be required for the physical office.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory sectoral license for hyper-casual mobile game publishing; optional municipal business registration (Gewerbeanmeldung) and no FINMA license required for pure ad-monetized publishing absent payment services or gambling features.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN / BAFU), with enforcement delegated to the cantonal environmental authority of the registered office.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - administrative office use only; no full Environmental Impact Assessment (UVP/EIA) required under Annex 1 to the Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (OEIA/OPV) for software publishers and mobile game studios.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial process wastewater; office discharges must comply with the Federal Water Protection Act (Gewässerschutzgesetz) and local sewer ordinances. Air quality thresholds under the Clean Air Ordinance (LRV/OPair) apply only to building ventilation systems, which in normal office operation remain below emission limits. Waste electrical and electronic equipment from IT infrastructure must be disposed through licensed collection systems under the Ordinance on Waste Disposal (VVEA/OLED) and WEEE regulations; packaging waste separation is mandatory.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance certificate issued by the cantonal fire inspection authority applicable to the leased office premises; structural load and evacuation capacity confirmed by the landlord's structural certificate for the designated office use; occupational safety and workplace clearance effected through Suva (Swiss National Accident Insurance Fund) or an approved insurer, including ergonomic workstations, first-aid facilities, and legally compliant emergency exits.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Federal Tax Authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC / Amministrazione federale delle contribuzioni AFC), Schwarztorstrasse 50, Berne; VAT registration and e-services portal: https://www.estv.admin.ch / Swiss VAT e-service 'SuisseTax' (E-Services de l'AFC). Cantonal tax authorities (Zug Tax Administration for the Zug Canton setting) handle cantonal/communal corporate income and capital taxes; the VAT is a federal indirect tax administered solely by the ESTV.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the Aktiengesellschaft via notarial deed, registered in the Commercial Register (Handelsregister) — the AG obtains the Swiss Business Identifier (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer UID / IDE / IDI, 9 digits), which is the statutory company tax ID for cantonal and federal income-tax purposes. Step 2: For VAT, apply online on the ESTV VAT e-portal using the UID; the ESTV issues a VAT number comprising the UID plus the MWST/IVA/TVA suffix and a validation code. Step 3: Because ad-monetization payouts from Google/AppLovin are legal services with foreign place of supply, the foreign entities' UID/foreign VAT IDs and contracts must be filed with the registration dossier. Step 4: Registration is retroactive to the date the CHF 100,000 worldwide turnover threshold is exceeded; voluntary registration is allowed below threshold but binds for at least 5 years. The UID/MWST number must appear on all invoices for taxable supplies and on receipts where Swiss VAT is charged.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: Resident Aktiengesellschaft is a separate taxable person subject to Swiss federal corporate income tax at 8.5% on net profit (effective federal rate after deduction of ordinary taxes: 7.83% due to federal tax being deductible as business expense; average combined federal/cantonal/communal effective rate in Zug about 14.5%). Modified Territorial_Scope: Swiss-resident AGs are taxed on worldwide income, but profits of foreign permanent establishments and foreign real estate are exempt under the applicable double-taxation treaty and the 'object exemption' (Objektbefreiung). No pass-through or fiscally transparent treatment applies; the AG is a per-se corporation with no partnership option. Capital tax imposed at cantonal level. Not a Tax_Exempt_Zone classification.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists; the AG is per se corporate. Statutory elections relevant to this digital-publishing AG: (1) Participation relief election (capital gains/dividend exemption) for qualifying shareholdings ≥10% — reduces effective rate on investment income; (2) Patent-box election and R&D super-deduction (150%) at cantonal level (Zug) via tax ruling; (3) Notional Interest Deduction (NID) election for cantonal tax purposes of qualifying finance functions; (4) VAT group taxation election under Art. 20 VAT Act for Swiss-consolidated entities; (5) Small-business exemption election: with worldwide turnover ≤CHF 250,000 and Swiss-taxable turnover ≤CHF 100,000, the AG may elect exemption from VAT even when the general threshold is exceeded solely through foreign B2B services (Art. 10 para 2 VAT Act, 2025 revision); (6) Flat-rate 'Saldo' simplified settlement procedure election under Art. 37 VAT Act (up to CHF 250,000 turnover). Hybrid mismatch elections: none available; Switzerland applies OECD BEPS Action 2-type rules and denies deductions for hybrid mismatches as of 2020 Finance and Tax Amendment Act.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) — Swiss VAT under the Federal Act on Value Added Tax of 12 June 2009 (Mehrwertsteuergesetz, SR 641.20), administered by the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 of worldwide turnover from taxable supplies (including services to foreign recipients) triggers mandatory VAT registration; from 1 January 2025, small businesses with world-wide turnover ≤ CHF 250,000 and Swiss-taxable turnover ≤ CHF 100,000 may remain exempt (for export-oriented service providers such as hyper-casual game publishers monetized through foreign ad networks).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, no continuous transaction control (CTC), no digital stamping and no mandatory e-invoicing clearance API in Switzerland. Invoices may be issued on paper or as structured e-invoices (eBill / QR-bill / EPUB; XRechnung not required). Mandatory invoice content under Art. 26 VAT Act: seller identity/UID-MWST number, buyer identity, description of service, consideration and applicable tax rate. For imports and exports, electronic customs declarations via the customs platform (e-dec / CargoTIS / transit TZS) are mandatory for goods; VAT on imported services falls under the reverse-charge mechanism of the recipient (Art. 45 para 3 lit. c VAT Act) with self-assessment in the periodic VAT return, eliminating the need for fiscal representation. The AG must maintain accounting records and e-audit accessible data; retention period 10 years under the Code of Obligations.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods export zero-rating: the 0% rate applies if physical goods leave Switzerland and the exporter substantiates export via the Swiss customs export declaration (Ausfuhrnachweis, art. 53 VAT Act). Offshore services (the dominant revenue stream: ad-network payouts from Google Ireland / AppLovin US, app-store royalties): Swiss VAT does not apply because the place of supply is outside Switzerland under Art. 21 para 2 VAT Act (B2B services supplied to a recipient located abroad); the AG must not charge Swiss VAT and must substantiate the customer's foreign place of business. The AG's input VAT on Swiss purchasing (development, cloud hosting, legal, marketing) is creditable only to the extent supplies are subject to Swiss VAT; mixed foreign/Swiss turnover requires an apportionment key (direct allocation and pro-rata) in the Swiss VAT periods. Refund of foreign VAT (e.g., EU VAT on AdMob commissions) cannot be claimed in the Swiss VAT return; Swiss input VAT refunds are paid quarterly by the ESTV.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration / Ausfuhrzollanmeldung (only for physical exports; digital game distribution does not trigger Swiss customs clearance)

Place-of-Supply Evidence Bundle for digital services: (i) written contracts with each ad-network (Google AdMob/AdSense, AppLovin/IronSource) stating recipient establishment in Ireland/USA; (ii) invoices listing the AG's UID-MWST number, counterparty's foreign VAT/GST ID and the service description; (iii) bank transfer statements / SWIFT MT103 inward remittance certificates evidencing cross-border settlement; (iv) customer business-status declarations (Bescheinigung über die Unternehmereigenschaft) or official extract from Irish/US tax registers confirming corporate status; (v) per-period 'list of services supplied abroad' submission for the Swiss VAT return.
Bill of Lading / Airwaybill for goods export scenarios
Inward Remittance Certificate — mirror of bank records confirming FX repatriation from the ad-network counterparty

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) / Direction générale de la Banque nationale suisse, administered operationally with the Swiss Federal Department of Finance; no separate foreign-exchange-control administration exists.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains full convertibility for both the capital and current account. The CHF is freely convertible and there are no general exchange-control restrictions on cross-border remittances, profit repatriation, or foreign shareholding. However, certain financial reporting duties apply to payments to and from persons domiciled abroad, primarily for balance-of-payments statistics; these do not constitute approvals or transfers of control.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender timeline or mandatory conversion ratio exists for export receipts in CHF or any foreign currency. Swiss exporters and holding companies may retain foreign currency on ledger, convert at freely traded market rates, or deploy funds into approved treasury instruments; only standard AML, tax-declaration, and statistical-reporting obligations apply.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Multi-currency Operational Transaction Account
Operational Account / Treasury Settlement Account with Capital Escrow Facilities
Operational Account and Dedicated Clearing Sub-account for Trade Disbursements

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW for principal bank-account use; MODERATE only as an auxiliary payout rail. Switzerland is not an EEA / EU member, and the EU EMI passport does not extend to Swiss territory. An offshore digital EMI, unless separately licensed by FINMA under the Swiss Banking Act (including the fintech licence under Art. 1b Banking Act) or acting through a Swiss-licensed partner bank, cannot lawfully hold client funds or operate a comprehensive Swiss clearing function. Offshore EMIs may be tolerated only for non-core transaction routing, subject to the Swiss company's own due diligence and strict segregation of funds.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is generally permitted for a Swiss-resident director or authorised signatory using FINMA-approved video-identification. For non-resident directors, most Tier-1 Swiss banks exercise discretion and may require a physical interview at the bank's head office in Switzerland or at a foreign private-banking subsidiary. Where a material beneficial owner resides in a third country with elevated AML concern, physical presence or an apostilled notarised identity and source-of-funds dossier is effectively mandatory. At least one natural person with a controlling role (e.g., director or senior manager) must be personally identifiable and subject to a live, verifiable interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Revenue inflows sourced from multi-territory digital advertising aggregators, including Google AdMob, AppLovin, and Unity Ads, without a single consolidated payment counterparty.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed platform service and payout addenda covering all ad monetisation channels; periodic settlement and payout statements from each platform; transaction-level reconciliation to the game back-end reporting; ISAE 3402 / SSAE 18 type-II reports issued by each major platform; audited GAAP financial statements of the Swiss AG; and a clear description of the revenue-share and ad-refund policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency, low-ticket micropayment velocity across the operating account, creating the appearance of split-transaction or batch-refund activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated daily technical reconciliation report between ad-server logs, the company's ERP or billing ledger, and bank credits; treasury policy on payment cycles; external audit confirmation on revenue completeness; and a narrative of the hyper-casual unit-economics and expected daily transaction volume.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border wire outflows to app-store operators, paytrail technical vendors, and game-production contractors in jurisdictions outside the DACH region, making Beneficial-Owner-of-Funds and purpose-of-transaction assessment non-standard.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully executed purchase orders, invoices, delivery certificates, and milestone sign-offs; transfer-pricing documentation under the Swiss Federal Act on Direct Federal Tax standards; board minutes approving treasury candidates and per-counterparty exposure limits; register of beneficial owners filed with the Swiss Central Commercial Office or Federal Office of Justice.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of a virtual IBAN, fintech digital account, or foreign EMI as a receiving/clearing point that creates a layered payment trail and obscures the final beneficiary settlement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal opinion from Swiss counsel assessing whether a FINMA licence or a licence exemption applies to the EMI; full screen of the EMI's AML compliance framework and internal audit findings; source-of-funds bank statements for each EMI transaction; an internal treasury directive that mandates direct account-to-account settlement with licensed banks where legally feasible; and a declaration of conformity to the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound routing uses SWIFT MT103 wire to the Swiss AG's CHF IBAN, preceded by a valid board resolution and shareholder capital payment mandate. For EUR inflows, use SEPA CT or TARGET2 settlement with IBAN referencing 'QR no purpose code' at some banks; for CHF, SNB payment system SIC is automatically used. The required purpose narrative must include 'Paid-in capital', 'Equity contribution', or 'Capital reserve payment' to distinguish from ordinary trade or loan funds. Verification requires the bank to confirm source-of-funds through investor's KYC file, a source-of-wealth declaration if the shareholder is an individual, and legal proof that the controlling shareholder is authorised to make the payment. No exchange-control approval is needed in Switzerland.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For vendor and contractor payments, Swiss corporates predominantly use SWIFT MT103 in EUR, USD, or CHF with real-time gross settlement (RTGS) via SIX xclear for domestic CHF; SEPA CT for EU EUR payees; and correspondent-bank-cleared MT103 or MT202 COV for non-Swift periphery banks. Commercial Letters of Credit under UCP600 are permissible for high-value procurement of hardware, SDK licensing, and media buying, particularly where Asian or Eastern-European payee banks demand documentary protection. Trade disbursements must observe the ORDO, FATF, and Swiss tax-at-source rules on royalties; no treasury repurchase or surrender obligation applies.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright Vanilla FX Forwards (deliverable) for EUR/USD/CHF and all fully convertible currency pairs, entered under ISDA/FXA documentation with FINMA-regulated or equivalent first-class banks.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for calendar-pegged or restricted-deliverability currencies (e.g., CNH, INR, KRW, BRL) where the underlying exposure is non-CHF revenue/street revenue from foreign app stores, with settlement in USD or EUR.
Cross-Currency Swaps (basis swaps) for matching medium-term balance-sheet assets and liabilities in foreign currency.

FX Options (vanilla put/call) used as stand-alone hedging instruments or within zero-cost straddles, subject to the bank's derivative-risk disclosure policy and the company's IFRS hedge-accounting election.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements and Management Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) via the federal central business register (Zefix)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year-end (Art. 958f OR). For a 31 December year-end: 30 June.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to CHF 1,000 after written reminder; repeated non-filing leads to court-ordered penalty and ultimate strike-off of the company (Art. 935 OR).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Direct Federal Tax and Cantonal Tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Authority of registered office and the Federal Tax Administration (ESTV)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally within 180 days after fiscal year-end (typically 30 June for 31 December balance-sheet date); extensions may be granted by the tax authority.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late interest of 4.5% p.a. from due date; administrative penalty up to CHF 10,000; potential assessment based on estimated income (Art. 174 DBG, Art. 206 StHG).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT Return and Settlement (Federal VAT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the end of the VAT period (quarterly or semi-annual for turnover > CHF 5,000,000; annual for turnover ≤ CHF 5,000,000). Annual deadline: 31 March of the following year for a calendar-year basis.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at 4.5% p.a.; fine up to CHF 8,000; repeated non-filing may lead to VAT licence suspension (Art. 101 MWSTG).

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary statutory audit required if a Swiss AG exceeds two of the following thresholds for two consecutive fiscal years: balance sheet total CHF 20 million; net revenue CHF 40 million; 250 full-time employees annual average. If not subject to ordinary audit, a limited audit (Review) applies unless the company has no more than 10 full-time employees and all shareholders approve in writing opting out (Art. 727 and 727a OR).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR) accounting rules; Swiss GAAP FER is recognised for large companies and required for listed entities; IFRS is permitted for qualified entities (Art. 958a OR).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Aktienbuch (share register) must remain current. The Swiss Register of Beneficial Owners (Register wirtschaftlicher Eigentümer) must identify natural persons holding more than 25% of shares or controlling votes. There is no annual UBO filing to a public authority unless a change occurs; however, the company must verify and confirm the accuracy of the UBO register at least once per calendar year in the absence of any change, and report any changes through the commercial register network (Zefix).
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors (board list and authorised signatories)
Minute Book (shareholder and board meeting minutes)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 – USD 3,500 per annum depending on canton and service provider
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 – USD 10,000 for a limited audit (Review); ordinary audit USD 12,000 – USD 45,000 when applicable

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% federal flat corporate income tax plus cantonal and communal income taxes; combined effective headline rate approx. 14.6% in Canton Zug and approx. 21.1% in City of Zurich for a resident AG.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holidays in Switzerland; R&D super-deductions available in several cantons, and the Swiss federal/cantonal IP patent box regime permits up to 90% exemption of qualifying IP-derived income; these incentives can reduce the in-regime effective tax rate to approximately 10% to 12% for qualifying software and gaming IP income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Canton Zug: 'Steuererklärung für juristische Personen' (Formular UZ) filed through the Zug Online Tax portal (eTax) for cantonal and federal direct tax; the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) applies through the same cantonal assessment. Separate federal tax registration applies for Swiss withholding tax and country-by-country reporting.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 6 months after the legal fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year AG the statutory filing date is 30 June of the following year, with extensions routinely granted to 31 December upon written request to the Zug Tax Office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total net income before tax as per statutory annual financial statements, including all operating profit from advertising monetization, in-app purchases, IP royalties, and other income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident AG with a Swiss permanent establishment or Swiss situs IP must report only Swiss-source income allocated under PE profit attribution rules; single-entity resident AG files on worldwide income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Participation income from qualifying subsidiary dividends, subject to Swiss participation relief; withholding tax on these dividends is recorded separately.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign residents with Swiss AG shareholdings report Swiss-source dividend income and may claim DTA participation relief / refund through tax return attachments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross royalty and license fees derived from third-country licensees, including payments for game software copyright, trademarks, and other IP exploitation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Swiss AG licenses IP to foreign ad-network platforms, the income is fully taxable in Switzerland as the beneficial owner; non-resident taxpayers with only foreign IP may file a limited return to claim treaty relief.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible business expenses, amortization of acquired software/IP, R&D costs, employee compensation, and arm's-length intercompany charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Swiss PE deductions must meet arm's length standards and are strictly limited to expenses economically connected to the Swiss PE; advance pricing agreements or TP documentation advisable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of Swiss withholding tax on dividends, interest on Swiss bank deposits and bond coupons; remitted to ESTV on Form 108.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign parent shareholders must provide TRC and DTA documentation to claim refund/reduced rate; treaty relief does not apply automatically.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final calculation of cantonal, communal, and federal profit tax payable after the application of participation relief, IP box deduction, and tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident taxpayers verify that all extraterritorial income is excluded and that treaty credits are claimed in the annexes to avoid double taxation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty up to CHF 10,000 per return plus default interest of approximately 4% to 8% per annum on assessed tax; tax evasion penalty up to 3 times the evaded tax; non-filing may trigger tax assessment by estimation plus immediate demand.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% final Swiss withholding tax imposed on gross Swiss-source dividends, payable regardless of beneficiary residence, with reductions only under an applicable DTA.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief, the foreign parent must obtain a DTA residency certificate (TRC) from its home tax authority, provide proof of dividend beneficial ownership (generally 10% or 25% shareholding and holding period per the applicable DTA), and submit Swiss Form 823 (refund route) or a provisional relief-at-source application to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration only after a specific DTA filing is admitted; pending TRC the 35% tax is withheld and refund timed 1 to 3 years after assessment.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: no Swiss statutory withholding tax on cross-border license fees; however, royalties paid to a controlling foreign shareholder may be recharacterized as constructive dividends subject to 35% WHT if not at arm's length. Interest: no Swiss withholding tax on ordinary trade loans or open-account financing; 35% Swiss WHT applies to interest from Swiss bank deposits, Swiss-issued bonds, and certain profit-sharing loans. DTA rates: dividends generally 0% to 15%, interest 0% to 10%, royalties 0% under Swiss tax treaties where relief is claimed.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CHF 900,000,000 group consolidated revenue triggers country-by-country reporting; no single statutory de minimis threshold for Master File/Local File is codified by ESTV, but Swiss TP documentation is required for all cross-border related-party transactions exceeding CHF 1,000,000 in services and CHF 5,000,000 in goods to satisfy contemporaneous documentation standards.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland has no separate UAE-style Economic Substance Regulation statute, but the OECD-conformed treaty abuse doctrine and the MLI Principal Purpose Test operate as a functional ESR: a Swiss AG must show actual entrepreneurial substance, active decision-making, qualified personnel, real offices, and assumption of operating/financial IP risk. Shell holding or IP-box companies without substance are denied treaty benefits, re-assessed under CFC rules, and exposed to mandatory arbitration and anti-abuse penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful submission of incomplete or false tax returns by under-reporting hyper-casual game advertising revenue, AdMob/AppLovin payout documentation, or IP licensing income, or destroying financial records and payout ledgers before the 7-year retention period.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty of up to 3 times the evaded tax plus default interest; criminal tax fraud (Steuerbetrug) subjects the taxpayer and responsible officers to fines up to CHF 50,000 and imprisonment up to 3 years under Swiss Federal Direct Tax Law Art. 186 and Swiss Criminal Code forgery provisions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, CEOs, and CFOs can be held jointly and severally liable for the tax shortfall when responsible for false declarations; they face personal criminal fines, disqualification from board positions during proceedings, asset seizure, foreign cooperation-based travel restrictions, and actual imprisonment of up to 3 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Empty Substance / Treaty Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a Swiss AG with no employees, no Swiss office lease, no board meeting minutes in Switzerland, and no risk-managing functions while booking high-margin game IP royalties enforceable only through a Swiss mailbox.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of DTA benefits under the MLI Principal Purpose Test, reclassification of royalties as disguised shareholder distributions subject to 35% withholding tax, full taxation in Switzerland plus 5% late interest, and administrative penalty of up to 3 times the adjusted tax; substance reassessment may also trigger profit reallocation to the foreign beneficiary.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly maintain a shell for treaty-shopping are personally liable for the incorrectly retained dividend WHT, can be sued for restitution by the tax administration, placed under a travel ban pending criminal investigation, and sentenced to imprisonment of up to 5 years under Swiss Criminal Code Art. 305bis for complicity in disguised transfers.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Money Laundering Through Payment Rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting large AdMob/AppLovin settlement payouts routed through opaque intermediary accounts without performing economic substance checks, failing to file a report under the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act (GwG) where the AG acts as a financial intermediary, or using in-app purchase proceeds to transfer criminal assets of behalf of organized groups.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the GwG, non-compliance can trigger supervisory fines of up to CHF 500,000 and confiscation of funds; intentional money laundering under Swiss Criminal Code Art. 305bis carries imprisonment of up to 5 years or a monetary penalty, with criminal forfeiture of all proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal criminal prosecution and imprisonment up to 5 years if they knowingly participated in laundering ad-network proceeds; travel bans, pre-trial asset freezes, and civil restitution orders are routinely imposed against the board; compliance officers and finance managers are equally exposed under Art. 29(g) GwG.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling or licensing hyper-casual game IP to a low-tax foreign affiliate at non-arm's-length prices without benchmarking, failing to prepare Master/Local File documentation, or deriving excessive deductible royalty payments from the Swiss operating entity to circumvent Swiss tax on advertising profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Swiss tax authorities may upwardly adjust taxable income to the arm's-length result, disallow excessive expense deductions, impose default interest of 4% to 8% annually, and add a penalty of up to 3 times the evaded tax; complete re-qualification of payments as constructive dividends triggers 35% WHT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for the 35% withholding tax uncollected where they approved constructive dividends; criminal transfer pricing misrepresentation can lead to personal monetary fines, seizure of Swiss bank assets, mutual assistance travel bans, and imprisonment of up to 3 years under Swiss tax fraud provisions.
